behavioral_intents: Detect masquerading of legitimate Windows system processes by running copies with system process names from user-writable directories instead of protected system paths.

Detect adversaries writing base64-encoded payloads into registry keys under HKCU\Software paths commonly modified by legitimate applications (Microsoft, Google, Mozilla, Adobe, Intel, Oracle) to persist code execution or configuration
Detect exfiltration of data to public paste/text storage services initiated by non-browser processes, which may indicate automated data stealing or C2 communication bypass.
Detect renamed system binaries or binaries with mismatched OriginalFileName metadata that indicate process masquerading attacks (T1036.005).
Detect exfiltration of sensitive data by scripting engines and utilities making outbound connections to public paste/text storage sites.

Detect adversaries using PowerShell to register and immediately modify scheduled tasks with elevated privileges, often originating from management/EDR parent processes to establish persistence or privilege escalation.
